task_1.title: Fix custom Context subclasses during inherited template rendering
task_1.description: Jinja 2.9.6 fixes a runtime regression where configuring a custom Context subclass on an Environment could break rendering of templates that extend another template containing variable expressions. The update restores correct variable resolution for inherited templates when a custom context class is in use.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that applications using a custom `Context` subclass through `Environment.context_class` can render inherited templates correctly when parent templates contain variable expressions, without failing during variable resolution.

expectation.grounded: When an `Environment` is configured with a custom `Context` subclass, rendering a template that uses `{% extends %}` must continue to resolve variables from the parent template correctly in fast resolve mode. Using a custom context class, including a simple subclass with no overridden behavior, must not cause rendering to fail with a runtime argument error during variable lookup.
expectation.conceptual: Custom template context classes should remain compatible with normal template inheritance. If a child template extends a parent template that reads variables, rendering should behave the same as with the default context and should return the expected output instead of failing at runtime.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve existing rendering behavior for default contexts and legacy custom-context handling while removing the regression specific to fast variable resolution with custom `Context` subclasses. Variable lookup semantics and rendered values for inherited templates must remain unchanged apart from eliminating the failure.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should only remove the regression for custom context usage and must not change normal rendering results or introduce new differences between default and custom context behavior.

behavior: An `Environment` that sets `context_class` to a custom `Context` subclass can render templates that extend another template without breaking parent-template variable resolution.
A parent template containing variable expressions is rendered successfully when reached through inheritance from a child template.
A custom context class that does not override any lookup behavior is treated as compatible with fast resolve mode and no longer triggers a runtime failure solely because it is custom.
Rendering returns the resolved variable value from the provided template context instead of aborting with an argument-related `TypeError` during lookup.
acceptance_criteria: When an application configures `Environment.context_class` with a subclass of `Context` and renders a child template that extends a parent template containing variable expressions, the render should complete successfully.
When the parent template references a variable provided to `render`, the rendered output should include the resolved value from that variable.
When the custom context subclass does not add any custom logic, rendering inherited templates should behave the same as with the default context implementation.
When inherited template rendering uses fast variable resolution, it should not fail solely because a custom `Context` subclass is configured.
